reader.title: Mobbing of Jack Minnicken
bases: A1 describes Black Democratic voters driven off a colored camp-meeting ground after the 1880 election, one 'set upon and mobbed' and one ordered to leave or be shot, for their votes; no injury is described, so political intimidation fits better than mob_assault.
Only the Orangeburg Democrat brief (A1) reports the episode; no other paper or follow-up was found.

summary.text: The mobbing of Jack Minnicken was an attack on a Black Democratic voter, who was "set upon and mobbed" off the grounds of a Black camp meeting in early November 1880, in a place the report did not name, likely near Orangeburg, South Carolina, where it was printed.
The Orangeburg Democrat, the only paper found to report it, said he was attacked for voting the Democratic ticket and tied it to a threat to shoot a second Black Democrat at the same meeting.
The attack followed the November 1880 election, at which Minnicken, described as "colored," had voted for the Democrats.
The paper placed the incident at a camp meeting held by Black worshippers but named no town, county or date beyond "a few days ago" before its issue of November 12.
According to the Orangeburg Democrat, Minnicken was set upon by a mob and driven off the meeting grounds because he "asserted his independence as a citizen" by voting as he chose.
The brief did not identify his attackers or describe any injuries.
At the same camp meeting, the paper said, a Black Democrat named Manny Robinson was visited by "a committee of eight Radicals" and told to leave the ground within two hours or be shot.
The paper wrote that his "only offence was voting the Democratic ticket."
No report of arrests, charges or any official response appears in the coverage found, and nothing further was printed about either man.

The episode survives in a single local item in the Orangeburg Democrat of November 12, 1880, a Democratic weekly that used the incident to portray "Radicals," the Republicans, as punishing Black men for political independence.
The item did not state the race of the attackers, though its setting at a "colored" camp meeting and its blame of the Radicals suggest the paper meant Black Republicans.
No other paper's version, reprint or follow-up was found.

accounts.label: Orangeburg Democrat local brief
accounts.gist: Minnicken was mobbed off a colored camp-meeting ground for voting Democratic, and Robinson was ordered off at gunpoint threat by eight Radicals for the same reason.

framing.detail: The Democratic weekly framed the mobbing as punishment of a Black man who 'asserted his independence as a citizen' and said Robinson's 'only offence was voting the Democratic ticket'.
